fixes.explanation: Building an altar is a fair guess, friend, but this passage never says Israel builds one. What it says is that Israel "…made a vow to the LORD…" (Numbers 21:2). A vow is a promise spoken to Him, and that's the answer here.

I can see why that came to mind, friend, since people do break promises. But Israel doesn't break this one. The vow was to "…devote their cities to destruction." (Numbers 21:2), and the text says "Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction…" (Numbers 21:3). This is a heavy part, but the text is clear that the vow was kept.

Putting things off is very human, friend, so I see why that one tempted you. But the text doesn't mention any delay here. It says the LORD delivered up the Canaanites, and "Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction…" (Numbers 21:3). This is a heavy part, but the text is clear that they kept the vow.

Perfect, baker! The text says "so they named the place Hormah." (Numbers 21:3). That comes right after the LORD heard Israel's plea and delivered up the Canaanites. Hormah is the name Israel gave the place.
